title: Shape and size errors: reading a traceback
hook: Core nodes often resize without telling you, and then a model refuses the result. Read the numbers in the error, and it usually says which two things disagree.

verified.claim: With a 128 by 64 gradient as second input, ImageBatch and ImageBlend kept values from 0.25 to 0.75, so they crop. LatentAdd did the same with a wide latent. JoinImageWithAlpha kept the full range, so it stretches.
The traceback shown is real, from LatentAdd given 4-channel and 16-channel latents on a CPU. We removed the long code lines of the engine's own frames.
LatentBlend gives the same size error, and LatentBatch gives: Sizes of tensors must match except in dimension 0. Expected size 4 but got size 16.

These core nodes resized without an error: ImageBatch 64+128 gave (2,64,64,3), ImageBlend gave (1,64,64,3), JoinImageWithAlpha with a 128 mask gave (1,64,64,4), LatentAdd gave (1,4,8,8), LatentBatch gave (2,4,8,8). ImageBatch of RGB and RGBA gave 4 channels.
ComfyUI adds a tip when a mat1 and mat2 error comes from a node with Sampler in its class name.
verified.ref: execution.py:execute, with a test node standing in for a sampler

verified.claim: The wording of each lab error comes from torch itself.
verified.ref: the lab, on the torch version in meta.json

unchecked: We didn't run a real model for the mat1 and mat2 or channel errors. We made the same torch errors with a small layer. Which real pairs of model and encoder cause them is from the tip's wording and from dimensions, not from a run.
The exact wording of torch errors can change between torch versions.
